name: Shelter
label: Revelation
lede: Ray Cappo shaved his head, took vows and left Youth of Today a Krishna devotee, then took a busload of monks on tour with a hardcore band. For a few years in the '90s the pit was full of tulasi beads.

eras.title: A farewell record, renamed
eras.text: Youth of Today was winding down and Ray Cappo had come back from India a Krishna devotee. He meant to make one final record about what he now believed, a farewell to punk's material world. Revelation Records heard it and decided it was a new band.

years.cap: Shelter's first record, out on Revelation the same year as Youth of Today's last album
years.h: Perfection of Desire comes out as Shelter, not as a Cappo solo record
years.p: Ray Cappo's goodbye to punk is a statement of faith, and Revelation puts it out as a new band. The name is the shelter a devotee finds in a guru and, finally, in Krishna.
years.xp:
The idea was vegetarianism and straight edge followed to the end of the road: a spiritual life. Cappo wrote the songs to say what he now believed, and Revelation made the call to release them under a band name.

The credits list the players by first name only. [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]], who had joined Youth of Today at 15, says he drummed two songs on that first release; Revelation's page credits a drummer named Bill.

Early footage survives: hate5six filmed a Shelter set on June 28, 1990, and Revelation has another from Club Revival in Philadelphia that December.

years.h: Live at Bunratty's, Boston, 1990

eras.title: Monks in the van
eras.text: Shelter became a traveling temple. The line-up changed constantly, with celibate devotees on one side and hardcore kids who liked the music on the other, and the shows mixed chanting, vegetarian food and a pit. Hardcore gave it a name, sometimes as a sneer: Krishnacore.

years.h: In Defense of Reality keeps the message up front
years.p: Shelter's second record doesn't soften the Krishna theology. Ray Cappo remakes the title track on the 2006 album Eternal.

years.h: Chris Interrante picks up the bass
years.p: Interrante plays bass in Shelter until 1993, and is back for the 2018 reunion.

years.h: Quest for Certainty is two line-ups on one record
years.p: Revelation's credits split it. Tracks 1 to 4 are [[Vic DiCara|a6698e1f-db17-4e93-9c4f-56678238e91f]], Chris Interrante and Eric Dailey; tracks 5 and 6 are [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]], Graham Land, a bassist credited as Yashomatinandana and a drummer listed as Sam.

years.h: Cappo sells Equal Vision, the label he started for Shelter
years.p: Ray Cappo founded Equal Vision Records in Albany in 1990 to get Shelter and other Krishna releases out. In 1992 he sells it to label manager Steve Reddy.
years.xp: The mission widened from there. Within a few years Equal Vision was putting out [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], Bane and [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]].

years.big: "Dudes in Krishna robes playing hardcore. It was punk, dangerous, and badass."
years.h: A 17-year-old books a tour from his bedroom
years.p: Sammy Siegler, drummer, on Shelter's tour with [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]]. He booked it off a phone list from Youth of Today's agent: devotees in a school bus, the Maharaja in a Winnebago, [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]] and the non-devotees in a van.
years.xp:
Siegler says the list of phone numbers came from Youth of Today's booking agent, Doug Caron, and he booked the tour at 17.

The guru the band called the Maharaja traveled in the Winnebago. To regulate who got to talk, Siegler brought a fluorescent orange hat called the Conch, passed hand to hand.

Inside Out's Vic DiCara crossed over too, playing guitar in Shelter and later forming [[108|7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b]].

yt: Live at The Factory, Wilkes-Barre, January 2, 1993
years.h: Attaining the Supreme says it in the title
years.p: Shelter's 1993 album states the mission in four words. The band also puts out two devotional side releases that year, Shelter Bhajan and Standard Temple Songs.

years.h: Porcell takes over on guitar and stays through 2000
years.p: Porcell, Ray Cappo's [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] partner, becomes Shelter's long-serving guitarist and, soon, its co-producer.

years.h: Norman Arenas joins on second guitar, with a zine on the side
years.p: Arenas joins for the Attaining the Supreme tour while editing the zine Anti-Matter. AllMusic says he later formed [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]], briefly rejoined Shelter, and ended up in New End Original.

eras.title: A metal label signs the robes
eras.text: By the mid-'90s Shelter sat among the biggest hardcore bands going, next to Snapcase, Strife, Earth Crisis and Sick of It All. Roadrunner, home of Type O Negative, signed them, and the band landed on festival stages with Slayer, Venom and the reformed Sex Pistols. It was as close to crossover as Krishnacore got.

years.big: "The article was all about how Krishnas brainwashed you."
years.h: Spin lays out the case against Krishna hardcore
years.p: Norman Arenas, then Shelter's guitarist, on the Maximum Rocknroll attack that Spin cites. The July 1995 feature adds that the gurus preach an authoritarian worldview a long way from anarchy.
years.xp:
The sharpest words came from inside the movement. Former [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]] singer [[John Joseph|64581915-b050-4a79-b1bf-29fdf6005093]] pointed to ISKCON's sex scandals and thievery, and to Monkey on a Stick, a book on the Krishnas' drugs, guns and murders.

Joseph told Spin his own spiritual master had sex with a 15-year-old girl. The piece carried no response from Ray Cappo to the cult charge.

yt: Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, October 27, 1995
years.h: Roadrunner releases Mantra, with a manifesto in the booklet
years.p: Eleven songs in about thirty minutes, produced by Tom Soares and Porcell. Ray Cappo's manifesto in the booklet, Supersoul, becomes the name of his imprint.
years.xp:
[[Dave DiCenso|fba8fbad-b75b-409a-8e91-4ef7cbb17605]] plays drums on the record. Sammy Siegler helped write the material but isn't on it; he told No Echo it came down to compensation disagreements with the band. The songs pair Krishna philosophy with a running critique of Western life, in titles like Civilized Man and Surrender to Your T.V.

Critics split along the obvious line. Trouser Press called Cappo a principled spokesman for transcendental thought set to a tough 4/4 beat. Germany's Ox-Fanzine, looking back, heard a tame rock album from another time.

years.h: Type O Negative and Shelter share a bill that "kind of worked"
years.p: Roadrunner labelmates Shelter and Type O Negative go on the road together. A devotee hosts them for dinner at a saffron-painted mansion.
years.xp: Siegler told No Echo the pairing blended metal, hardcore and even hip-hop. Of Type O's singer: "Pete was cool, I think we ate birthday cake together on his birthday somewhere."

years.h: Brazil for the first time, and a Beatles cover as a bonus
years.p: Shelter play Brazil in 1996. The Brazilian edition of Mantra adds two bonus tracks, one of them the Beatles' We Can Work It Out.

years.h: Beyond Planet Earth is the last Roadrunner album
years.p: Shelter's second Roadrunner album is also their final one for the label. By now the band tours North America, Europe and South America.

years.h: A sleeping driver puts the van off a Colorado cliff
years.p: On the Beyond Planet Earth tour, Shelter's driver falls asleep. AllMusic says everyone survives, but some band members are seriously injured and take months to recover.

eras.title: Twenty summers, then quiet
eras.text: By the turn of the century the Krishna wave in hardcore had crested, and Shelter pulled back from full-time preaching. Two albums on two labels, a last run of shows, then a hiatus nobody called a breakup.

years.h: Victory Records releases When 20 Summers Pass
years.p: Shelter move to Victory for their 2000 album. It's also the year Porcell's first run in the band ends.

years.h: The Purpose, the Passion goes out on Cappo's own Supersoul
years.p: Shelter tour Europe and the eastern U.S. behind the record, then go on extended hiatus.

eras.title: The door never quite closed
eras.text: Shelter came back in pieces: a European tour, a Cappo record under the band's name, a pair of one-off shows on two continents. Cappo had moved to California by then; he'd later settle in upstate New York as a yoga teacher.

years.h: Europe, 2003, where the audience never left
years.p: A reunion tour takes Shelter back to Europe.

years.cap: Ray Cappo singing with Shelter, July 2006
years.h: Eternal is a Cappo record with the Shelter name on it
years.p: Essentially a Ray Cappo solo album under the band's name: ten new songs plus a remake of In Defense of Reality. A European tour follows.

years.cap: Cappo with Youth of Today, Garage Saarbrucken, September 2010, the band he was also reuniting
years.h: The first reunion show is in Gothenburg
years.p: Shelter play Gothenburg, Sweden, the first of two reunion shows ten days apart, on either side of the Atlantic.

years.cap: Cappo with Youth of Today, Brooklyn, October 2011
years.h: Ten days later, Reading, Pennsylvania
years.p: Shelter's second 2011 reunion show is back home in the U.S.

eras.title: Punk to monk, then the Dome
eras.text: The classic players regrouped, Cappo wrote it all down, and Mantra came back on vinyl at thirty. In 2026 Shelter is billed as the other half of a Youth of Today night.

years.cap: Cappo with Shelter on stage, June 2016, two years before the classic line-up returned
years.h: Cappo, Porcell, Siegler and Interrante play Shelter again
years.p: Ray Cappo, [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]], [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] and Chris Interrante play a U.S. tour and a European festival. Siegler is back on drums twenty-eight years after Perfection of Desire.

years.h: From Punk to Monk arrives with a foreword by Moby
years.p: Ray Raghunath Cappo's memoir comes out on Mandala Publishing.

years.h: Mantra turns thirty on vinyl
years.p: An anniversary vinyl edition puts Shelter's 1995 Roadrunner album back in record stores.

years.h: London's Dome books Cappo for two nights, both bands
years.p: Ray Cappo is billed to front [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] and Shelter, the band he started when Youth of Today ended.
